title: Out-of-core / distributed Boolean F4
original_requirement: Complete next m4 cells beyond n<=15 ell<=5 memory wall with distributed/out-of-core Boolean F4 or GPU-HBM Macaulay reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Profile construction, symbolic preprocessing, elimination and fill-in separately.
Complete m4 ell6,7 and guess-count ell8,9 frontier cells; preserve older degree7 closures as separate requested trials.
Small controls agree exactly; checkpoint/restart, peak memory, disk/network traffic and full resource accounting.
remaining_gaps: Host has16GiB and no GPU; cited18-50GB cells exceed available RAM without an implementation change.
Implement serializable elimination checkpoint, row/block streaming, bounded resident storage and distributed/GPU kernel; ordinary sparse in-memory elimination is not out-of-core.
Local RUNPOD_API_KEY missing; remote credential availability is not known from local environment.
execution_note: Commands are source bindings, not launch receipts; preserve original trials and output to a fresh location through the applicable runner. No official approval or status transition is implied.
original_audit_text: Distributed or out-of-core Boolean F4. The entire binary verdict rests on extrapolating D from n ≤ 15 and ℓ ≤ 5, and the next cells died at 18 to 50 GB. The blocker is memory engineering, not mathematics. A multi-node block reduction or a GPU-HBM Macaulay pass is the single highest-leverage measurement in the program.
